# Service holder proof v1: local codec and origin verification

This additive source slice implements the fixed `secs-service-holder-proof-v1` challenge/proof codec and public-key origin/binding verification. It does not implement native service provisioning/custody, a Wallet service presenter, challenge/context signing, issuance, coherent authority/evidence loading, journal/replay consumption, installed transport admission or qualification. Gate 1 remains open. Synthetic fixture success and native owner inputs do not grant installed production authority.

`core::service_holder_proof` is verifier-free and key-free. Every public wire constructor and decoder is untrusted. `server::service_holder_proof::verify_service_holder_proof_v1` returns a private-constructor `AuthenticatedServiceHolder`, with immutable claims and challenge/whole-Packet SHA-256. It proves origin and matching bindings relative to the independent native owner inputs; it is neither an evidence approval nor a replay or context-signing capability. Repeated verification intentionally succeeds while current inputs/window remain valid; the future store must consume the challenge atomically.

## Fixed profile and exact bytes

Only `runtime-v1` / `runtime://receiver-local` and `service-v1` / `service-management` are supported, with fixed `native-plaintext-request-v1`. Runtime uses the existing frozen 28 full operation/opcode pairs. Service uses its 12 full operations with explicitly native-allocated opcode >=0x40; manifest and receiver-policy checks bind the actual allocation. Requests cannot select trusted profiles, operation namespaces, policy, key material or descriptors.

The request is the exact UTF-8 byte sequence in Packet.encrypted_payload, not encrypted in this explicit native IPC profile. Length and SHA-256 plus both signed transcripts bind it without reserialization. Core validates framing/bindings; the native guard re-parses through the frozen public static reader and derives operation/resource independently. Finite decimal/exponent/large integer lexemes and Runtime opaque NUL bytes remain exact. Service retains its existing bounded static reader constraints. Neither the pure parser nor this slice attests receiver SDK canonical encoding; exact producer/receiver admission vectors remain required.

Existing Packet v0 layout, generic caller-proof-v1, human Wallet paths and context schema 4 are unchanged. The new profile alone requires MAC=all zero. Old v1 decoders reject its tag; no generic ingress learns the new profile. Request limits remain Runtime 2,097,152 and Service 65,536 bytes. Compact proof <=16,384 bytes excludes duplicate request bytes. Inner binary signed challenge <=application request maximum+16,384; the future canonical JSON/base64 Wallet facade is not implemented.

## Canonical signed and wire encoding

`F(name,value) = u16BE(name byte length) || ASCII name || u32BE(value byte length) || exact value`. Names/order are closed; missing, duplicate, reordered, oversized, truncated and trailing fields reject before authentication. Numbers are u64BE, digests raw32, opcode one byte, signatures64, challenge ID32, session16 and nonce12. Metadata is printable ASCII without whitespace/control characters: issuer/holder node/key/subject references <=128, audience/full operation <=200, resource <=1,024 and handler <=256; dev/ handlers deny.

Issuer transcript: `b"secs-service-challenge-v1/signature\0" || fixed claims || F(request_bytes, exact raw request)`.

Holder transcript: `b"secs-service-holder-proof-v1/signature\0" || F(issuer_signature,64) || F(holder_policy_digest,32) || exact issuer transcript`.

The compact proof starts `b"secs-service-holder-proof-v1\0"`, then fixed claims, then issuer_signature, holder_policy_digest and holder_signature. The inner signed challenge uses the exact issuer transcript followed by F(issuer_signature,64). It is a bounded binary inner representation, not the future outer challenge transport.

The 36 fixed claims are, in order:

`profile, application, payload_mode, issuer_node_id, issuer_key_id, audience, operation, resource, opcode, request_length, request_sha256, schema_bundle_sha256, descriptor_fingerprint, handler_id, holder_subject_id, holder_key_id, holder_public_key_fingerprint, receiver_policy_digest, permission_policy_digest, registry_snapshot_digest, required_evidence_digest, evidence_snapshot_digest, evidence_observations_digest, evidence_adapter_profiles_digest, evidence_source_epoch_digest, evidence_valid_not_before, evidence_valid_until, evidence_observed_at, evidence_revocation_checked_at, evidence_revocation_fresh_until, challenge_id, session_id, nonce, ttl_seconds, issued_at, expires_at`.

The public bundle preimage is `b"secs-service-public-contract-bundle-v1\0"`, F(application, runtime-v1/service-v1), F(each schema filename, raw SHA256 of exact schema file) in filename order, F(reader_profile, `secs-service-call-contract/v1`), F(reader_source_sha256, raw SHA256 of exact reviewed static reader src/lib.rs). Runtime has runtime-v1.schema.json; Service has service.command.v1.schema.json then service.query.v1.schema.json. A schema or reader source change changes the bundle and requires new challenge/proof/release expectations. Independent Python hashlib/struct golden preimages and digests pin both application bundles in the public fixture directory.

## Whole-window guard and independent native inputs

TTL is nonzero and <=60; issued_at>0, expires_at-issued_at=TTL, all finite time bounds fit the JavaScript safe unsigned integer domain. Challenge/session/nonce must not be all zero. Current acceptance is issued_at<=final_now<expires_at. The entire immutable [issued,expires) window must fit explicit current holder/issuer key windows, Wallet validity, receiver policy/principal/allow/future-deny limits, and independently loaded typed evidence validity and revocation-freshness horizons. Equal exclusive ends are allowed; shortening or resetting an already signed window is never allowed.

The receiver policy prepares the whole original window and must return exactly its signed expiry/bindings. The actual current PermissionPolicy is evaluated for every integer second of the <=60-second window, covering future denies and allow gaps. The current native manifest's fingerprint (native descriptor:sha256: prefix decoded to raw32), handler, full operation, nondev production target and TTL are checked. This target label remains insufficient authority by itself.

CurrentServiceProofState borrows native registries/manifest/receiver/permission policy and independent owner pins: permission and registry snapshot digests, complete typed evidence bindings, Wallet policy digest/finite validity, and exact recorded challenge-transcript digest. Do not construct those pins by copying submitted claims. Evidence snapshot/required obligations/observations/adapter profiles/source epoch digests and all five finite evidence times must match the independent owner snapshot exactly. This slice does not compute/qualify their provenance or freshness: the future coherent snapshot, typed evidence adapters/current guard and recorded challenge store must do so, including restart lineage, actual descriptor obligations, current cached-delivery revalidation and final clock after blocking checks. Its successful result does not waive that work.

Issuer and holder verification uses strict Ed25519 with native owner public keys; supplied key references are lookups only. Both keys require active status, ed25519 algorithm and explicit finite exclusive validity windows containing the full signed window. Effective revocation and issuer replaced_by deny; issuer node/purpose and native production admission metadata are independently checked. No JSON production flag is loaded here. Holder public fingerprint and registry snapshot pin prevent proof-selected key replacement/epoch changes.

## Initial service registry and rotation semantics

Both narrowly scoped service registries are bounded at32 input records and preserve the generic registries/v1 behavior. Any duplicate key ID or repeated public material under multiple IDs/nodes/subjects rejects the **entire** constructor, so unrelated entries cannot remain usable from a rejected registry. Distinct active public keys for one stable holder subject are allowed. Issuer and holder public material must also be disjoint across their current service registries. Stable-subject store quotas are future journal work. Revoked/replaced keys, changed key fingerprint or changed registry epoch require a new challenge/proof. The future owner loader must coherently publish rotations; no live identity changes are implemented.

## Public fixtures and remaining admission

`server/tests/fixtures/service-holder-proof-v1` contains synthetic public challenge, proof, issuer/holder transcripts, Packet and Ed25519 public-key bytes for Runtime and Service; no private key bytes are exported. Disposable deterministic seeds/signing exist only under cfg(test). The test-only update switch regenerates those fixture files; there is no production signing oracle. Fixtures exercise exact numeric lexemes/opaque Runtime NUL and explicit synthetic Service allocation, not installed trust or qualification. Independent bundle vectors have full source/schema digests.

Required subsequent work remains: native coherent evidence/policy/custody loader; bounded typed issuer/challenge/context signing and Wallet holder facade; all-state bounded transactional challenge journal, cached-delivery guard/replay/crash/clock tests; native provisioning/rotation/revocation; result attestation producer and target admission. Preserve the reviewed context/challenge TTL equality and 2MiB public Runtime payload. The retained total-Packet, SDK/HTTP/authority/stdin amendments are being implemented and reviewed separately by Runtime and Service; full installed producer/receiver compatibility and authority qualification remain required. Current generic workflow Gate8 qualification is separate from Gate1; isolated installed macOS qualification and target evidence are still required.
